one_line: Ruler of Calicut and his admiral Kunjali III during the 1571 siege of the Portuguese fort at Chaliyam.

appearance.age_look: The Zamorin appears as a dignified, broad-shouldered man in his late 40s; Kunjali III as a lean, battle-hardened man in his mid-30s.
appearance.face: The Zamorin has an oval face, medium-brown Malabar complexion, calm large eyes, neatly groomed moustache and short beard, with a composed, strategic expression; Kunjali III has a sharper jaw, slightly darker complexion, trimmed moustache and goatee, intense eyes and a focused, determined look.
appearance.hair: The Zamorin’s black hair is medium length, oiled and pulled back into a low knot at the back of his head under a simple gold-bordered white cloth headband; Kunjali III’s black hair is also tied back into a tight knot, partially covered by a dark indigo turban wrapped low and compact with a narrow white band edge.
appearance.costume: The Zamorin wears a long-sleeved ivory cotton angarkha-style tunic reaching mid-thigh with a subtle woven texture, over a gold-bordered white mundu (dhoti) wrapped to the ankles; across his chest is a rich deep-red silk shawl draped from left shoulder to right hip, and he has a broad, plain gold waistband, simple layered gold necklaces, slim gold bangles, and a thin gold armlet on his right upper arm; his feet are in brown leather sandals. Kunjali III wears a fitted dark indigo cotton jama-style tunic with long sleeves and side slits, reaching the knee, over a narrow white cotton lungi wrapped and knotted at the front, falling to the ankles; a sturdy brown leather belt with a simple brass buckle holds a small utilitarian pouch, and he has a muted dark-red cotton sash tied diagonally from right shoulder to left hip; jewellery is minimal—a single plain silver ring and a slim black thread amulet at the neck—and he also wears brown leather sandals.
appearance.signature: The Zamorin carries an unadorned, straight steel talwar with a simple disc pommel and minimal brass hilt, sheathed at his left hip; Kunjali III carries a slightly curved, well-used steel talwar with a plain iron hilt and disc pommel at his left hip and grips a rolled parchment map of the Chaliyar river mouth in his left hand.

ref_desc: The Zamorin has an ivory tunic, gold-bordered white mundu, deep-red silk shawl and plain steel talwar, while Kunjali III wears a dark indigo jama over white, brown leather belt, muted red sash and carries a worn steel talwar and river-map parchment, all in ivory, deep red, gold, dark indigo and brown.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body anime-style male figures standing side by side as a model sheet: the Zamorin on the left, with a medium-brown Malabar complexion, oval face, calm large eyes, neat moustache and short beard, black hair pulled into a low knot under a simple gold-bordered white cloth headband. He wears a long-sleeved ivory cotton angarkha-style tunic to mid-thigh with subtle woven texture, a gold-bordered white mundu wrapped to the ankles, a rich deep-red silk shawl draped from left shoulder to right hip, a broad plain gold waistband, layered simple gold necklaces, slim gold bangles and a thin gold armlet on his right upper arm, and brown leather sandals; at his left hip is a sheathed straight steel talwar with minimal brass hilt and disc pommel. On the right, Kunjali III has a slightly darker complexion, sharper jaw, intense eyes, trimmed moustache and goatee, and black hair tied into a tight knot under a compact dark indigo turban edged with a narrow white band. He wears a fitted dark indigo cotton jama-style tunic with long sleeves and side slits to the knee over a narrow white cotton lungi to the ankles, a sturdy brown leather belt with brass buckle and small pouch, and a muted dark-red cotton sash running from right shoulder to left hip, plus brown leather sandals; at his left hip hangs a slightly curved worn steel talwar with plain iron hilt and disc pommel, and in his left hand he holds a rolled parchment map of the Chaliyar river mouth. Keep proportions and energy shonen anime-style but costumes, weapons and jewellery historically grounded, using ivory, deep red, gold, dark indigo and brown leather as the dominant colours, shown clearly from head to toe for consistent redrawing.
